leads.title: Criminal Code of Nicaragua - Articles 168, 170, 172 and 175
leads.documents: Legality of same-sex sexual activity since March 2008; age of consent 16 regardless of sexual orientation or gender; all sexual offenses gender-neutral
leads.detail: Cited as articles 168, 170, 172 and 175 of the Criminal Code of Nicaragua

leads.title: Constitution of Nicaragua, Article 72 and Family Code (effective 8 April 2015)
leads.documents: Non-recognition of same-sex marriage, stable unions, partnerships and adoption; marriage defined as voluntary agreement between a man and a woman
leads.detail: Article 72 quoted verbatim; Family Code approved June 2014, effective 8 April 2015; action of unconstitutionality filed

leads.title: Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACHR) Advisory Opinion of 9 January 2018
leads.documents: Regional human-rights machinery requiring states party to American Convention to grant same-sex couples access to all family registration including marriage with all derived rights, without discrimination
leads.detail: Issued 9 January 2018; cites Articles 1.1, 2, 11.2, 17, 17.1 and 24 of the American Convention

leads.title: Penal Code, Article 315 on offenses against labor rights
leads.documents: Employment discrimination protection; discrimination based on sexual option punishable with up to one year in prison
leads.detail: Cited as Article 315 of the Penal Code

leads.title: Law No. 820 for the Promotion, Protection and Defense of Human Rights in the face of HIV and AIDS (Ley num. 820)
leads.documents: Anti-discrimination protection based on sexual orientation under Article 3(l)
leads.detail: Cited as Article 3(l) of Law No. 820

leads.title: Ministerial Resolution 671-2014
leads.documents: Prohibition of discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression in access to health services
leads.detail: Cited as Article 1 of Ministerial Resolution 671-2014

leads.title: Penal Code, Article 36(5) - hate crime aggravating circumstance
leads.documents: Sentencing enhancement when crime motivated by discrimination based on sexual orientation
leads.detail: Cited as Article 36(5) of the Penal Code

leads.title: Center for Justice and International Law - 2012 survey on aggressions 1999-2011
leads.documents: Documented enforcement/violence: 53 aggressions against LGBT people, including 15 murders (10 gay men, 4 transgender people, 1 lesbian); notes under-reporting
leads.detail: 2012 survey by the Center for Justice and International Law covering 1999-2011

leads.title: Programa Feminista La Corriente - quarterly and annual reports of violence 2021-2024
leads.documents: Ongoing documented incidents and enforcement pattern: assaults, hate crimes/murders, suicides, sexual assaults, extortion; majority against trans women; perpetrators include family, strangers, state police; locations street/home
leads.detail: 2021: 67 assaults, 1 hate crime/murder, 2 suicides; 2022: 39 assaults, 3 hate crimes, 1 suicide; 2023: 35 assaults, 2 hate crimes, 1 murder, 1 suicide, 2 sexual assaults, 1 extortion; 2024 Q1-Q2: 13 assaults, 5 hate crimes, 1 missing

leads.title: United Nations joint statement on ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity (2011)
leads.documents: Nicaragua's international rights posture after 2008 decriminalization; condemnation of violence/discrimination against LGBT people; government urging repeal of sodomy bans including Antigua and Barbuda
leads.detail: Signed by Nicaragua in 2011 at the United Nations
